entries.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
entries.summary: Three drawn positions of a dumbbell Romanian deadlift, seen from the side.

provenance.positions: Authored for this repository from its own curated execution instructions and coaching cues for movement_id 88 (packages/core-db/src/schema/017_movement_batch.sql, 025_movement_coaching_content.sql).
instructionAgreement: stand — "Stand with dumbbells resting on the front of your thighs."
hinge — "Push your hips straight back and let the dumbbells slide down your legs, knees softly bent"; the hips travel back while the knees stay softly bent.

bottom — dumbbells drawn at mid-shin with a flat back, the depth the instructions describe as "until the hamstrings tell you to stop"; the load stays against the legs, per "daylight between them and you means the load has wandered onto your back".
provenance.artwork: No third-party artwork. Every frame is a list of joint coordinates in this file, drawn at runtime from plain React Native views.
provenance.licence: Original work created for this repository; covered by the repository licence.

entries.reviewNotes: Side view only. Bottom depth varies with hamstring length; the drawn depth is one common range, not a target. No qualified technique reviewer has signed this off yet.
entries.limitations: Three frames cannot show the moment the back starts rounding, which is the real stopping signal in the instructions.

entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository after owner review: a neutral upright start between the two low stacks (ruling 4), hips travelling on the exact thigh circle and the torso rotating on the exact spine so knees extend with the hips on the drive, arms long to the handles throughout, and the near cable running to a low pulley just ahead of the toes. entries.name: Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics.
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the knees bent a good deal and the torso stopped well short of level. Source-bound side-view draft: the bar lies across the back of the shoulders with the hands on it; the hips travel back and the straight trunk lowers until it is about level with the floor, then the hips come forward to stand tall. The knees keep the one soft bend they start with for the whole rep, so the legs only lean back with the hips. The bar is seen end-on. Not drawn: the rack, and the shoulder-width stance, which a side view cannot show.
entries.summary: With the bar across the back of the shoulders and the legs still, push the hips back and lower a straight torso to about level with the floor, then bring the hips forward to stand tall.

entries.name: Band Good Morning

entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: a side-view hip hinge with a long band under the mid-foot and across the back of the shoulders, held at the front with elbows soft. entries.reason: Source-bound draft whose text is a draft written from the public-domain free-exercise-db entry and its photographs (supplemented by the companion One-Arm Kettlebell Snatch and Kettlebell Swing entries where the source instructions array is empty), awaiting the owner (the catalogue's own text is a placeholder on a source hold).
